title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving primary health care services to El-nino at risk population in Beletweyne District of Hiran region

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gtltspan style="font-family: Calibri, sans-serif font-size: 10pt"gtThe proposed project will run for nine months and support 22,000 individuals. The direct beneficiaries of the project are 1980 pregnant and lactating women, 4400(2244 girls and 2156 boys) under five children, 21,300 (7654 males and 8435 females). Through this initiative, WARDI will operationalize one health facility and three mobile teams that will cover 15 villages and IDP camps that have little or no access to health. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gt
lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gtltspan style="font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtThe proposed project will provide life-saving primary health care services that include the provision of emergency free consultation services for both under five and over five, treatment of common illnesses, provision of essential medication and supplies, antenatal and postnatal services, immunization, skilled birth attendant and newborn care, provision of emergency reproductive health services, social behavior change, and messaging through the engaged community health workers who will do disease surveillance and reporting to reduce the spread of communicable disease at the community level.ltspan style="color:black"gt lt/spangtSimilarly, the proposed intervention will be integrated with MHPSS and GBV services into the primary health care services to improve the physical and well-being of the flood affected communities in the target area. lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gt
ltspan style="font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtWARDI will use a community-based participatory approach to develop community capacities through increasing capacity among its own employees, local authority personnel, MoH staff, and CHWs to ensure the project's sustainable future. To better coordinate humanitarian operations and prevent duplication, the proposed project will complement other programs in the target area, such as nutrition, education, washing, child protection, and food security, implemented by WARDI, Save the Children, DRC, and Mercy USA.WARDI will coordinate and reach out to other partners through coordination meeting, mapping of beneficiaries and creating an effective referral pathwaylt/spangt
